PORTRAIT ROUTING - READ FIRST
When Appearance begins with the exact header `## IMPORTANTMANDATORY USER-SUPPLIED COMPOSITION LOCK`, return the entire Appearance unchanged as the final prompt and stop: no prepending, appending, summarizing, restyling, or reframing. Everything below applies only to generated NPCs without that header.

SOURCE
Render `visualDescription` as the character. Where it is absent or silent, fall back to the NPC’s `type` and its `## Visual Description` block, then to visible facts in `basicInfo`; the type’s body always holds. Never expose or infer from `hiddenInfo`. Character Creator Image Styles apply to player Appearance only. This configuration owns style, lighting, and framing; the record owns everything else.

WORLD STYLE
Dsar's Modern Anime Style. Clean 8K anime production artwork: bold line work with visible weight variation, tapering strokes, clear silhouette separation, and large organized shapes readable at a glance. Build applicable hair from large defined clumps with clean interior partitions, not strand detail. Render clothing as clear garment panels and readable layers, folds following the body, without adding or replacing garments. Use clean cel shading with a decisive two-to-three step ramp, hard shadow terminators, and sharp material separation. Faces carry anime production finish: clean eye rendering with defined highlights, controlled skin gradients, no photographic pores or texture overlay. Use Astravael anatomy; Chorus retains its host species. Keep the science-fiction identity. Prefer character-design accuracy over photorealism, painterly texture, AI gloss, and micro-detail noise. Style controls rendering only, never identity, anatomy, colors, outfit, or pose.

VISUAL-NOVEL FRAME (required unless a complete frame is supplied)
One 3:4 vertical waist-up visual-novel portrait at natural eye level, framed from the natural waist or just below to the top of the head or hair silhouette, keeping face, neck, shoulders, chest, and major outfit construction in canvas. The subject fills about 82-88 percent of image height, centered or subtly offset. Hands appear only when the pose brings them in. Signature props enter only when the source makes them visible and stay secondary to the face. Never widen past waist-up, tighten to a face-only or chest-up crop, or use an extreme angle, action shot, or wide cinematic composition. For unusual nonhumanoids use the closest coherent waist-up equivalent.

LIGHTING
Controlled anime-structured cinematic lighting motivated by the scene. Establish one dominant key light and take its direction, colour, and height from a real source in the setting. Add restrained environmental fill, negative fill so cel-shadow masses stay readable, selective rim light where a real source supports it, and reflected light from nearby surfaces. Preserve exact supplied colors under all of it: light changes value, not hue identity, and a costume's authored colour must remain identifiable in shadow. Give major materials distinct cel-shaded responses so cloth, skin, metal, glass, energy, fur, and chitin never share one finish. Keep the face the brightest readable area unless the scene forbids it. Lighting improves form, depth, and focal hierarchy; it never redesigns the character, invents a source, or pushes toward photorealism.

RENDER FIDELITY
Draw exactly what the source states and add nothing: no weapon, armor, uniform, scar, aura, glow, rune, portal, companion, or power effect it does not establish. Where the source fixes a choice the species allows to vary, that choice is final: never substitute another option the type permits. Never humanize nonhuman anatomy or alienize a Starian or Human: human ears, natural human skin that no hair, eye, outfit, House or light colour reaches. Never drop, duplicate, or restyle a permanent marker. Keep supplied colors, materials, placement, left-right detail, and count.

SCENE
Use the environment the source states; with none stated, a neutral science-fiction space with two to four objects and unmarked surfaces, never a blank gradient, skyline, battlefield, portal, or cosmic field. Keep the character dominant and the environment secondary.

SINGLE SUBJECT
Exactly one character in frame. Never add a second figure, bystander, crowd, silhouette, reflection, companion or background personnel, and never depict a character the request did not name, including one named in nearby narration, availability guidance, faction lists, or story instructions. If the source names more than one, render only the subject of the request.

QUALITY CONTROL
Keep limb count, hand and finger structure, proportions, and prop count correct, with believable hand-to-object contact. No duplicate bodies, merged limbs, floating props, or invented garments.
End every NPC prompt with exactly:
No text, lettering, words, labels, logos, signatures, watermarks, poster borders, character-card layouts, interface elements, numbers, or random writing anywhere in the image.

# AREA IMAGE CONFIGURATION

Generate one finished environmental illustration of the exact authored area inside its parent location. The area is the subject. It must feel like a specific navigable place within the larger location, not a second image of the entire location and not a generic room, street, or landscape.

## SOURCE ORDER
Use visible information in this order:
1. Manual area image prompt or explicit visual description.
2. Exact area key and its `description`.
3. Parent location `name` and the visual sections of `basicInfo`.
4. Parent region for climate, geography, and exterior light.
5. Restrained defaults only when required information is absent.

Higher sources override lower ones. Never illustrate `hiddenInfo`, secrets, encounters, occupants, or story state. Area `paths` identify adjacency only. Do not render path names as signs, invent corridors, or display a map from them.

Use Dsar's Modern Anime environmental style: clean high-resolution anime production background art, bold controlled linework, large organized shapes, crisp silhouettes, cel-informed shading, sharp material separation, cinematic lighting, and premium anime environment finish. Avoid photorealism, painterly texture, AI noise, and micro-detail clutter.

## AREA IDENTITY
Show the exact function and identity described for the area. Preserve its parent location's architecture, materials, technology, culture, condition, color logic, and recurring anchors while giving this area its own recognizable layout and focal feature.

The parent location provides continuity, not permission to copy every landmark into the frame. Include one to three parent-location anchors only when naturally visible or structurally repeated. Do not replace the area with a wide exterior of the parent location.

## COMPOSITION
Use an eye-level or gently elevated environmental view suited to movement and interaction. Establish a clear entrance or approach, usable floor or terrain, a primary focal zone, and visible circulation deeper into the area. Use foreground, middle-ground, and background separation.

For interiors, show room scale, doors or openings, functional zones, furniture, equipment, structural supports, and physical light sources. For exterior districts, show street or path scale, nearby facades or terrain, boundaries, and a limited glimpse of the parent location beyond.

Do not use a top-down map, blueprint, floor plan, cutaway, collage, split panel, extreme aerial view, or character-focused composition.

Small anonymous figures or vehicles may establish scale only when appropriate and must remain secondary. Do not add named characters, crowds, combat, active powers, portals, disasters, or story events unless explicitly supplied.

## ENVIRONMENT DETAIL
Describe supported:
- Immediate architecture or terrain.
- Surface materials and condition.
- Two to five function-specific objects, fixtures, or systems.
- Clear foreground interaction space.
- Middle-ground focal activity zone without invented people.
- Background continuation, doorway, corridor, skyline glimpse, or landscape.
- Physical light sources, time of day, weather, and atmosphere.

Keep materials sharp, silhouettes intact, and the layout understandable. Use atmospheric depth without obscuring the navigable space. Do not add clutter unrelated to the area's purpose.

## CONSISTENCY
Preserve the parent's established Astravael architecture and local cultural identity. Do not invent signs, flags, faction emblems, holograms, machinery, magical effects, damage, decay, overgrowth, or security systems unless supported.

Keep screens, plaques, doors, signs, banners, walls, equipment, vehicles, clothing, and surfaces free of readable writing. Logos or emblems appear only when explicitly required and remain nonverbal symbols.

## VISUAL GOAL
End the descriptive prompt with one sentence stating what makes this specific area recognizable within its parent location and what activity or atmosphere the space visually supports.

## AVOID
Block whole-location replacement views, generic rooms or streets, incorrect parent architecture, unsupported people or events, invented connections, empty composition, unusable layout, blank gradients, excessive fog, blur, muddy materials, noisy detail, broken perspective, readable writing, borders, UI, and map labels.

End every area prompt with exactly:
No text, lettering, words, labels, logos, signatures, watermarks, poster borders, map labels, interface elements, numbers, or random writing anywhere in the image.

## READING basicInfo
Read visible architecture, materials, layout, scale, light and access from Nexara's prose or visual headings. Ignore occupants, secrets, activities, social pressure and story state. Read authored region terrain, climate and sensory details without requiring fixed headings. Preserve geography and local technology; salvaged construction remains advanced science fiction.

# LOCATION IMAGE CONFIGURATION

Generate one finished environmental illustration of the exact location. The place is the subject; do not turn it into a character portrait, map, poster, title card, or generic city image.

## SOURCE ORDER
Use visible information in this order:
1. Manual location image prompt or explicit visual description.
2. Exact location key, `name`, and the visual sections of `basicInfo`.
3. Authored area names and descriptions for internal variety.
4. Parent region for climate, geography, skyline, and terrain.
5. Restrained defaults only when required information is absent.

Higher sources override lower ones. Never illustrate `hiddenInfo`, secrets, occupants, encounters, or story state. Paths and connections describe navigation, not visible signs or roads unless supported.

Use Dsar's Modern Anime environmental style: clean high-resolution anime production concept art, bold controlled linework, large organized shapes, crisp architectural silhouettes, cel-informed shading, sharp material separation, cinematic lighting, and premium anime background finish. Illustrated rather than photorealistic, painterly, or texture-noisy.

## LOCATION IDENTITY
Lead with the exact architectural, geographic, cultural, technological, magical, cosmic, or natural identity. Preserve supplied era, materials, climate, terrain, scale, condition, color logic, and recurring visual anchors.

Do not replace a specific location with a generic skyline, castle, laboratory, forest, street, planet, headquarters, or battlefield. Do not combine unrelated landmarks. Faction influence may appear only through supported architecture, materials, vehicles, or emblems; do not invent propaganda, crowds, uniforms, flags, or readable signs.

## COMPOSITION
Use a wide environmental composition with foreground, middle-ground, and background. Show both the major silhouette and grounded surface-level detail. Architecture, terrain, and environmental systems carry the frame.

Use one clear focal structure or geographic anchor, supporting secondary structures, navigable space, and enough surrounding context to understand the setting. Keep perspective coherent. Do not use a top-down map, globe view, cutaway, floor plan, collage, split panel, fisheye distortion, or extreme aerial distance unless a manual prompt requires it.

Small incidental figures or vehicles may establish scale only when appropriate. They remain anonymous, secondary, and visually minor. Do not feature named characters, crowds, combat, active powers, portals, disasters, or story events unless explicitly supplied.

## ENVIRONMENT DETAIL
Describe supported architecture, terrain, water, vegetation, streets, paths, interior surfaces, two to six defining objects or systems, foreground materials, middle-ground organization, background skyline or horizon, physical light sources, time of day, weather, and atmosphere.

For interiors, show an inhabitable space with entrances, circulation, work zones, furniture, machinery, or systems appropriate to its function. For exteriors, show approach, boundaries, surrounding terrain, and recognizable landmark scale.

Use atmospheric depth without blur or haze swallowing detail. Keep materials crisp. Use weather and lighting only when supplied or strongly implied.

## CONSISTENCY
Preserve Astravael architecture and established city identities without copying unrelated places. Keep technology, magic, and alien construction culturally consistent. Do not invent floating objects, holograms, runes, energy, damage, decay, or overgrowth unless supported.

Keep screens, plaques, signs, banners, monuments, vehicles, clothing, and surfaces free of readable writing. Logos or emblems appear only when explicitly required and remain nonverbal symbols.

## VISUAL GOAL
End with one sentence stating what makes this exact location immediately recognizable and what atmosphere it communicates.

## AVOID
Block generic replacement environments, wrong geography or era, mixed architectural identities, unsupported characters or events, random monuments, empty composition, blank gradients, excessive fog, blur, muddy materials, noisy detail, broken perspective, duplicate structures, readable writing, borders, UI, and map labels.

End every location prompt with exactly:
No text, lettering, words, labels, logos, signatures, watermarks, poster borders, map labels, interface elements, numbers, or random writing anywhere in the image.

## READING basicInfo
Read visible architecture, materials, layout, scale, light and access from Nexara's prose or visual headings. Ignore occupants, secrets, activities, social pressure and story state. Read authored region terrain, climate and sensory details without requiring fixed headings. Preserve geography and local technology; salvaged construction remains advanced science fiction.
